entries.title: Meeting highlights from the Committee for Veterinary Medicinal Products (CVMP) 6-8 October 2026

entries.summary: The CVMP gave a positive opinion, under exceptional circumstances, for a marketing authorisation of Bovilis Lumpyvax.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams working on veterinary vaccines must monitor this approval and update their dossiers accordingly.

entries.label: EMA Guidelines
entries.title: Questions and answers on the PIP compliance verification procedure at EMA, and on paediatric rewards
entries.description: Questions and answers on the PIP compliance verification procedure at EMA, and on paediatric rewards
entries.summary: EMA clarifies the procedure for verifying compliance with the Paediatric Investigation Plan (PIP) and explains how paediatric rewards are awarded.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams responsible for paediatric development must understand the verification steps to ensure PIP compliance and eligibility for rewards.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Notice of Compliance (NOC) Data Extracts
entries.description: The data extract is a series of compressed ASCII text files of the Notice of Compliance (NOC) database.
entries.summary: Data extracts of the Notice of Compliance database are now available.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams should be aware that the NOC database is accessible via compressed ASCII files for reference.

entries.label: EMA News
entries.title: Clinical trial applications advice pilot becomes permanent
entries.description: The Accelerating Clinical Trials in the EU (ACT EU) advice pilot, which helps sponsors prepare clinical trial applications, will become a permanent initiative from January 2027…
entries.summary: The ACT EU advice pilot for preparing clinical trial applications becomes a permanent initiative effective January 2027.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams sponsoring EU trials will now have ongoing, standardised guidance available, requiring them to integrate ACT EU advice into their pre‑submission workflow.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Product monograph brand safety updates
entries.description: Product monograph brand safety updates for Submissions cleared between 01-09-2026 and 30-09-2026
entries.summary: Brand safety updates for product monographs submitted in September 2026.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must review and incorporate updated safety information into their submissions.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide to reporting and providing information on drug shortages and discontinuations (GUI-0120)
entries.description: This document is intended to help market authorization holders comply with sections C.01.014.8 to C.01.014.91 of the Food and Drug Regulations
entries.summary: Provides guidance on reporting drug shortages and discontinuations per sections C.01.014.8 to C.01.014.91 of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.why_it_matters: Market authorization holders must comply with these reporting requirements, so RA teams must ensure timely submission of shortage and discontinuation information.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide to distributing drugs intended for the Canadian market for consumption or use outside Canada (GUI-0145)
entries.description: This document is intended to help drug establishment licence holders comply with sections C.01.014.94 to C.01.014.95 of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.summary: The guide explains how drug establishment licence holders must distribute drugs for use outside Canada in compliance with sections C.01.014.94 to C.01.014.95.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams responsible for export distribution need to ensure processes meet these regulatory sections.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide on the exceptional importation and sale of drugs in response to shortages and discontinuations (GUI-0148)
entries.description: This document will help drug establishment licence holders comply with sections C.10.004 to C.10.013 of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.summary: Provides guidance on how drug establishment licence holders can import and sell drugs during shortages and discontinuations.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must review import/export procedures to ensure compliance with C.10.004 to C.10.013 and adjust their supply chain accordingly.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide on extending expiration dates of marketed drugs in response to drug shortages (GUI-0500)
entries.description: This document will help market authorization holders and drug establishment licence holders understand how to comply with sections C.010.014 to C.10.021 of the Food and Drug Regulations
entries.summary: Provides guidance for extending expiration dates of marketed drugs during shortages
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory teams must ensure compliance with C.010.014 to C.10.021 to maintain drug availability during shortages

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Register of Innovative Drugs
entries.description: A listing of drugs pursuant to sub-section C.08.004.1(9) of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.summary: A new Register of Innovative Drugs has been established under sub-section C.08.004.1(9) of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory Affairs teams need to ensure their products are included in or compliant with this register, impacting drug registration and approval processes.

entries.label: EMA Guidelines
entries.title: European Medicines Agency pre-authorisation procedural advice for users of the centralised procedure
entries.description: European Medicines Agency pre-authorisation procedural advice for users of the centralised procedure
entries.summary: The EMA has issued procedural advice for users of the centralised procedure to help navigate its pre‑authorisation requirements.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams applying for centralised marketing authorisation should read the guidance to ensure their submissions comply with the updated procedural expectations.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Drug Product Database data extract [2026-10-05]
entries.description: The Drug Product Database (DPD) extract files contain complete product information for all approved, marketed and cancelled products, for human, veterinary, disinfectant and radiopharmaceutical use.
entries.summary: A new Drug Product Database (DPD) data extract now contains complete information for all approved, marketed and cancelled products across human, veterinary, disinfectant and radiopharmaceutical uses.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must access this updated database to ensure product dossiers and regulatory submissions are based on current information for all product categories.

entries.title: Advice on ‘end-of-year’ submission dates for type I variations in 2026
entries.description: Marketing authorisation holders wishing to receive an outcome in 2026 should submit type IA annual updates, individual type IA and type IAIN variations, and super-groupings…
entries.summary: The update specifies new end‑of‑year submission deadlines for type I variations in 2026.
entries.why_it_matters: Marketing authorisation holders must align their submission schedules to meet the 2026 deadline for type IA updates and type IAIN variations.

entries.label: EMA News
entries.title: EMA Management Board: highlights of September 2026 meeting
entries.description: Mid-year report 2026 from the Executive DirectorEMA presented results and achievements of its operations for the first half of 2026 to the Management Board. Between January and…
entries.summary: No regulatory changes were announced at the EMA Management Board meeting.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory teams can continue following existing procedures without modification.

entries.label: EMA News
entries.title: Global regulators call for advancing alternatives to animal testing across the medicine lifecycle
entries.description: EMA has endorsed a joint statement from the International Coalition of Medicines Regulatory Authorities (ICMRA) calling on medicine developers, manufacturers, regulators and…
entries.summary: Global regulators endorse advancing alternatives to animal testing across the medicine lifecycle.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams in all therapeutic areas must evaluate how this policy change impacts their development and regulatory submissions, particularly regarding the use of non‑animal methods.

entries.label: EMA News
entries.title: Executive Director speech at EMA women’s health multi-stakeholder workshop
entries.description: Amsterdam, 28 September 2026Check against delivery (The published text is based on the prepared speech. Minor differences may have occurred during delivery)Good morning,…
entries.summary: New regulatory guidance will be issued to enhance the inclusion of women in clinical trials for medicinal products.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams across all therapeutic areas must review trial designs to ensure adequate representation of female participants and comply with forthcoming EMA requirements.

entries.label: EMA News
entries.title: Women are missing from medicines development: EMA’s roadmap for change
entries.description: By the end of 2026, EMA will develop a regulatory roadmap to help drive decisive change on how women’s health is considered across medicines development and regulation. This…,         Women are still missing: from research and data, prevention, diagnosis and treatment. But the momentum to improve support for women’s health has never been stronger.…,         Meaningful change starts with dialogue and with a shared understanding of the challenges we face. We end this workshop with a clear path to action”, “National regulatory…,   The multistakeholder workshop, broadcast live, brought together over 100 leading voices on women’s health at EU and international level, from regulators to patients, healthcare…
entries.summary: EMA will develop a regulatory roadmap by the end of 2026 to ensure women's health is better considered in medicines development and regulation.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must be aware that future regulatory expectations will require more robust inclusion and analysis of women in clinical studies and product dossiers.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Updated Register of Certificates of Supplementary Protection and Applications
entries.description: Listing of drugs pursuant to sub-section 120(1) of the Certificate of Supplementary Protection Regulations.
entries.summary: The register of certificates of supplementary protection has been updated.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams should monitor the updated list to ensure accurate tracking of SP certificates for affected products.

entries.label: EMA Guidelines
entries.title: Member states contact points for review of national implementation of quick response (QR) codes of veterinary medicinal products authorised via the centralised (CP), mutual recognition (MRP), decentralised procedures (DCP) and national procedures
entries.description: Member states contact points for review of national implementation of quick response (QR) codes of veterinary medicinal products authorised via the centralised (CP), mutual recognition (MRP), decentralised procedures (DCP) and national procedures
entries.summary: Member states have designated contact points to review national implementation of QR codes for veterinary medicinal products authorised through centralised, mutual recognition, decentralised, and national procedures.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams should note the designated contact points for coordination and ensure QR code implementation aligns with national regulations.

entries.title: INS-GCP-1 procedure for coordinating good-clinical-practice inspections requested by the CHMP

entries.summary: Introduces a new procedure for coordinating GCP inspections requested by the CHMP.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams must be aware that inspections can now be coordinated through this procedure, ensuring timely preparation and compliance.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Monthly update to the generic submissions under review list
entries.description: This is a list of certain generic drug submissions currently under review. The Generic Submissions Under Review list includes the medicinal ingredient(s) and therapeutic area. Downloadable Excel files are included.
entries.summary: This update releases the current list of generic drug submissions under review.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams should review the list to monitor which generic applications are pending and ensure compliance with review timelines.

entries.label: EMA Guidelines
entries.title: Substances considered as not falling within the scope of Regulation (EC) No. 470/2009, with regard to residues of veterinary medicinal products in foodstuffs of animal origin

entries.summary: Regulation (EC) No. 470/2009 is now excluded from certain veterinary medicinal product residues in animal foodstuffs.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must revise residue monitoring and reporting procedures for the affected substances.

entries.why_it_matters: RA teams developing medical devices can now consult directly with MHRA for guidance on regulatory requirements.

entries.title: Pharmacovigilance-related regulatory recommendations for centrally authorised veterinary medicinal products during 2026
entries.description: Pharmacovigilance-related regulatory recommendations for centrally authorised veterinary medicinal products during 2026
entries.summary: New pharmacovigilance recommendations have been issued for centrally authorised veterinary medicinal products effective in 2026.
entries.why_it_matters: Veterinary regulatory affairs teams must update their pharmacovigilance procedures to align with the new guidance.

entries.title: Compliance and enforcement policy for health products (POL-0001)
entries.description: This policy describes Health Canada's national compliance and enforcement approach for health products regulated under the Food and Drugs Act and its regulations.
